title: Cost learning and strategic inventory: who should carry inventory in a vertical supply chain?
summary: Problem Definition: In a decentralized supply chain, the downstream retailer (he) may strategically carry inventory to induce lower future wholesale prices, triggering the upstream manufacturer (she) to raise the early-period wholesale price to deter such behavior. In the presence of cost learning, where future production cost declines with cumulative early-period production, the manufacturer faces a key trade-off. To accelerate cost learning, should she lower the early-period wholesale price to encourage larger retailer orders and downstream inventory carryover, or should she instead overproduce in the early-period and hold inventory herself, bearing the holding cost? Methodology: We develop a game-theoretic model to capture such supply chain interactions in the presence of the manufacturer’s cost learning and the retailer’s strategic inventory. Results: We characterize the conditions for different inventory holding patterns in the supply chain, where only the manufacturer, only the retailer, both, or neither carries inventory. Countering the established notion that a manufacturer should hold inventory to enhance cost learning when her holding cost is low, our research reveals that she should abstain from holding any inventory, even at zero holding cost, when the retailer’s holding cost is sufficiently low. Further, we show that the manufacturer should completely refrain from holding inventory as an instrument to accelerate learning, irrespective of the retailer’s holding cost, when there is no uncertainty associated with cost learning or when the learning benefits are realized continuously. Managerial Implications: Our results guide manufacturers experiencing cost learning to determine their inventory decisions based on cost learning features and the retailer’s holding cost.
topics: Supply Chain Resilience and Risk Management

title: Who Directs the Control Tower? Customer vs. Supplier-Managed Inventory in Supply Chains
summary: Information distortion and incentive misalignment often undermine supply chain performance. In response, many firms adopt a “control tower” approach, whereby one party assumes responsibility for replenishment decisions across the supply chain. Industry examples showed that this role may be assigned to the customer, Customer-Managed Inventory (CMI), or to the supplier, Supplier-Managed Inventory (SMI). This paper investigates when one governance structure is preferable. We study a two-echelon, one-to-many supply chain consisting of a single supplier and a customer operating multiple warehouses. We characterize optimal base-stock policies and equilibrium holding-cost-sharing parameters under CMI and SMI and benchmark them against decentralized operations and a fully centralized system. Two primary forces shape the choice between CMI and SMI: the relative shortage penalty costs of the two parties and the structure of the customer’s distribution network. Specifically, CMI is preferred when the customer faces relatively higher shortage penalties and operates in a more asymmetric environment—for example, when demand is concentrated in a subset of its warehouses or when replenishment lead times vary substantially across these locations. In contrast, SMI is favored under opposite conditions. We further examine how intertemporal and interspatial demand correlations affect this comparison. A key finding is that, although neither CMI nor SMI achieves the first-best outcome, their efficiency loss relative to full centralization is typically small. Calibrated numerical studies based on four industry cases disentangle the incremental value of information sharing, decision-right transfer, and cost sharing, showing that most performance gains stem from decision-right transfer supported by appropriate holding-cost sharing. This paper was accepted by Jayashankar Swaminathan, operations management. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02137 .

title: The Effect of Lead Directors on Corporate Social Responsibility
summary: Abstract Drawing on insights from the compromise board leadership structure theory, which posits that the presence of a lead independent director on corporate boards enables management to maintain unity of command through consolidated leadership and autonomy while also ensuring effective oversight, we theorize that this balance creates an equilibrium in which the firm is more likely to achieve stronger corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance. We further propose that improved financial flexibility serves as the economic mechanism through which the main effect operates. We also posit that these collaborative efforts are expected to contribute to superior long‐term firm performance. Additionally, we argue that women in the influential role of lead independent director bring distinctive qualities to the board that further enhance firm outcomes in this context. Our findings, robust to potential endogeneity concerns, are consistent with these propositions, underscoring the significant impact of board structure and female leadership in a key position on advancing CSR performance and firm profitability.

title: Consolidating circular economy, resilience and sustainability indicators for healthcare supply chain modelling
summary: Analytical and simulation-based models rely on explicitly defined indicators to specify objectives, constraints, and outputs, shaping the trade-offs models reveal and the decisions they support. While supply chain modelling has traditionally prioritised efficiency, cost, and service level, disruption risks and environmental and social pressures have increased interest in circular economy, resilience, and sustainability (CERS). However, CERS indicators remain fragmented and are rarely operationalised in an integrated manner within modelling. This gap is particularly salient in healthcare supply chains (HSCs), where system complexity, societal criticality, and disruptions intensify trade-offs between CERS objectives. This study investigates how CERS objectives are operationalised in HSC modelling and explores their perceived importance in practice. A multi-method research design was adopted. First, a scoping review of 135 papers, indexed in Web of Science and Scopus, synthesised how CERS indicators are embedded in objectives, performance indicators, constraints, and experimental parameters in HSC models. Second, a healthcare-focused expert elicitation, including interviews and a rating exercise, interpreted and prioritised literature-derived indicators. The review identified 102 literature-derived indicators and 17 additional practice-informed indicators. Findings highlight imbalance in indicator coverage and identify potential trade-offs, with economic indicators dominating and social-related indicators underrepresented despite their practical significance. The study consolidates findings into a modelling-aligned CERS framework and illustrates how selected indicators can support modelling studies and trade-off analysis. The framework provides a structured basis for developing integrated CERS-informed HSC models.

title: AUDIT, DISCLOSURE AND TRANSPARENCY: LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE IMPERATIVES IN NIGERIA
summary: ABSTRACT: Audit, disclosure and transparency are the tripod of credible corporate governance, reducing agency costs, information asymmetry and market abuse in public companies. In Nigeria, recurring corporate failures such as Cadbury, Afribank, Intercontinental Bank and Oando despite clean audit opinions raise questions on the efficacy of legal framework. The study examines audit, disclosure and transparency imperatives under Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, Investments and Securities Act 2007, Financial Reporting Council Act 2011, Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018 and NGX Listing Rules. The study adopts doctrinal research methodology, relying on primary sources of statutes, subsidiary legislation, case law and secondary sources of textbooks, journal articles and reports, with comparative reference to UK, US and South Africa. The study finds that Nigeria has robust laws mandating independent audit, continuous disclosure and sustainability reporting, yet enforcement is weak due to concentrated family ownership, regulatory fragmentation among CAC, FRCN, SEC and NGX RegCo, compromised auditor independence, low shareholder activism and voluntary ESG compliance. Law on paper is globally aligned but law in practice is deficient. The study recommends strengthening FRCN into a PCAOB-style independent oversight board, reducing audit rotation from 10 to 5 years, harmonizing disclosure through a single electronic portal with automated sanctions, activating institutional investor activism and mandating audited ESG and integrated reporting.

title: Emerging Trends in Financial Reporting and Accountancy: Digital Transformation, Sustainability, and Regulatory Dynamics
summary: Abstract The landscape of accountancy and financial reporting has undergone a monumental shift driven by rapid technological advancements, evolving regulatory frameworks, and increasing demand for corporate transparency. This research paper examines the convergence of automation, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Sustainable Financial Reporting (ESG disclosures) within modern accounting practices. title: Digital Supply Chain Traceability and Supply Chain Resilience in Sri Lankan Apparel Exporters: The Mediating Role of Operational Decision-Making Speed
summary: Supply chain resilience has emerged as a critical capability for firms operating in increasingly fragile, uncertain, and disruption-prone global supply networks. For export-oriented industries such as apparel, the ability to respond rapidly and recover effectively from disruption is central to sustaining competitiveness. In this context, digital supply chain traceability (DSCT) has become an important digital capability because it enhances the capture, tracking, and retrieval of critical supply chain information across sourcing, production, and distribution activities. Yet, despite growing interest in digital transformation, existing research has paid limited attention to DSCT as a distinct organizational capability and has provided insufficient explanation of how it is associated with resilience outcomes. This study addresses this gap by examining the association between DSCT and supply chain resilience (SCR), with operational decision-making speed (ODMS) examined as a mediator, in apparel exporting firms in the Western Province of Sri Lanka. Drawing on Organizational Information Processing Theory and the Dynamic Capabilities View, the study examines the associations among DSCT, ODMS, and SCR. Survey data were collected from managerial and executive-level employees (N = 210) and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate significant positive associations between DSCT, ODMS, and SCR, with ODMS partially mediating the association between DSCT and SCR. These findings suggest that the strategic value of traceability extends beyond visibility and transparency, as DSCT is also associated with faster operational decision-making and stronger resilience. The study advances resilience literature by identifying a process-based explanation linking digital capability and resilience, while providing actionable implications for apparel exporters seeking to develop more responsive and robust supply chains.

title: Artificial intelligence decision support system for small business supply chain resilience under uncertainty
summary: Small-business supply-chain studies often report forecast improvements without showing how calibrated demand and logistics uncertainty should change feasible replenishment decisions. This study evaluates an uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence decision support system implemented as an auditable benchmark architecture that couples leakage-safe forecasting, conformal demand intervals, calibrated ex-ante logistics-delay probabilities, a conditional-value-at-risk stochastic linear program, and calibration-frozen ABC-XYZ policy assignment. The constituent methods are established; the contribution is their explicit and separately testable coupling from prediction to constrained prescription. The analysis used 350,000 FreshRetailNet-50 K records and 120 store-product series, DataCo for logistics-risk estimation, and UCI Online Retail for external robustness. XGBoost improved mean absolute error by 2.74% over a seven-day moving average. Under the baseline scenario weights, the risk-adjusted program achieved 3.93% stockout and 95.53% aggregate service and significantly outperformed fixed reorder, EOQ, forecast-only, and risk-neutral optimization after Holm correction, but it did not differ significantly from the adaptive policy. Reoptimization under equal, routine-heavy, and disruption-heavy probability profiles preserved policy non-dominance but changed the LP-adaptive relationship, demonstrating sensitivity to probability beliefs. AI-only retained the highest service and EOQ the lowest cost across all profiles. The results establish a context-dependent cost-resilience frontier rather than universal AI superiority.

title: Capital market liberalization and corporate financing efficiency
summary: Using A-share listed firms in China from 2008 to 2024, this paper examines the effect of capital market liberalization on corporate financing efficiency. The results show that capital market liberalization significantly improves financing efficiency, and the finding is robust to a battery of robustness checks. Mechanism analyses indicate that liberalization improves the information environment, stock liquidity, and external monitoring. The analysis of heterogeneity shows that the effect is stronger for non-state-owned firms and for firms with lower managerial myopia, weaker internal governance, and lower organizational inertia.

title: Analyzing the Implementation Pathways of Blockchain Technology-Enabled Supply Chain Resilience in the Manufacturing Industry
summary: Against the backdrop of escalating geopolitical conflicts, public health crises, and demand volatility, manufacturing supply chains face mounting disruption risks, while traditional management approaches exhibit persistent limitations in information transparency, trust building, and coordinated response. Existing research has largely focused on isolated applications and lacks a comprehensive analysis of the mechanism linking technical characteristics, intermediary capabilities, and supply chain resilience. This study examines how blockchain technology enables supply chain resilience in the manufacturing sector through a systematic literature review and theoretical analysis, supplemented by illustrative industry cases. Drawing on empirical and analytical studies published between 2018 and 2026, the paper identifies three core implementation pathways: enhanced information transparency and real-time sharing to strengthen predictive and adaptive capacity; smart-contract-enabled collaboration to improve cross-organizational coordination; and end-to-end traceability to strengthen risk management and accelerate recovery. Cases such as BMW's PartChain initiative and Walmart's blockchain traceability system demonstrate these pathways in practice. The analysis further reveals that blockchain effectiveness is contingent on capacity level and demand uncertainty. Deployment costs, interoperability gaps, and data privacy concerns constrain broader adoption. The study concludes with targeted countermeasures for firms, industry consortia and regulatory authorities, alongside suggestions for future research directions.

title: From gravity models to supply chain resilience: a bibliometric analysis of free trade agreement research
summary: Purpose This study examines the evolution and intellectual structure of research at the intersection of free trade agreements (FTAs), gravity models, and supply chain resilience. It aims to determine how resilience- and logistics-oriented perspectives have developed alongside traditional gravity-based trade research and to assess the extent to which these research streams are becoming conceptually integrated. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted using scientific publications indexed in Scopus between 1995 and 2026. The study combines performance analysis and science-mapping techniques, including keyword frequency analysis, co-word network analysis, centrality measures, thematic mapping, and life-cycle analysis. These methods are used to identify the field’s intellectual structure, dominant research themes, conceptual linkages, and emerging directions. Findings The results show that gravity models remain the principal analytical foundation of FTA research, while trade agreements, trade liberalization, and international trade continue to constitute the core of the field. Supply chain management emerges as an important bridging concept connecting this established trade-policy literature with more specialized themes related to resilience, risk, sustainability, and disruption. The findings therefore suggest a gradual broadening of the research agenda from conventional assessments of trade creation and efficiency toward questions of vulnerability, shock transmission, adaptation, and recovery. They also highlight growing opportunities to incorporate logistics-related dimensions, such as trade continuity, supplier dependence, transport reliability, and network resilience, into future gravity-based evaluations of trade agreements. Originality/value This study contributes by systematically identifying the conceptual and methodological bridge between gravity-based FTA research and supply chain resilience and logistics research, two streams that have largely developed in parallel. It shows how established gravity-based approaches can provide a foundation for future research assessing not only whether FTAs increase trade and market access, but also whether they influence supply-chain exposure, adaptability, and recovery under external disruptions.

title: Corporate Governance and ESG Compliance in India: A Critical Analysis of Emerging Business Law
summary: Abstract Corporate governance and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) compliance have emerged as important components of modern business regulation in India. Traditionally, corporate governance focused primarily on accountability, transparency, protection of shareholder interests and responsible management. However, the contemporary business environment requires companies to consider a broader range of environmental and social stakeholders. ESG principles have therefore become increasingly integrated into corporate decision-making, disclosure, risk management and investment practices. In India, this transformation is reflected through the Companies Act, 2013, Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulations, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) provisions and the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) framework. SEBI introduced BRSR to strengthen sustainability-related disclosures by listed entities and to provide more measurable and comparable information regarding environmental and social performance. Subsequently, SEBI introduced BRSR Core, which focuses on selected key performance indicators and reasonable assurance, with implementation being progressively extended to larger listed entities and aspects of their value chains. This research critically examines the relationship between corporate governance and ESG compliance in India. It analyses the emerging legal framework, identifies implementation challenges, evaluates the role of boards and management, and proposes measures for improving ESG accountability. The study adopts a doctrinal and analytical research methodology based primarily on legislation, regulatory materials, policy documents and secondary literature. The research finds that ESG is gradually moving from a voluntary sustainability concept towards an important component of corporate accountability and business law.

title: Green Innovation, Green Supply Chain Management, and Environmental Performance in Ghana’s Agro-Processing Sector
summary: Background: Agro-processing firms face growing pressure to reduce the environmental impacts associated with resource use, production, packaging, transportation, and waste generation. Green supply chain management and green innovation have emerged as important organisational approaches for improving environmental performance. However, limited empirical evidence exists on whether green innovation strengthens the relationship between green supply chain management and environmental performance, particularly within Ghana’s agro-processing sector. Aims: The study examined the relationship between green supply chain management (GSCM) and environmental performance, assessed the relationship between green innovation (GI) and environmental performance, and examined the moderating role of GI in the relationship between GSCM and environmental performance in Ghana’s agro-processing sector. Study Design: Quantitative explanatory research design. Place and Duration of Study: Ghana’s agro-processing sector. Data were collected from employees of agro-processing firms during the study period. Methodology: Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Convenience sampling was used to select respondents with knowledge or experience in supply chain management, environmental practices, or innovation. Of the 100 questionnaires administered, 96 usable responses were obtained, representing a 96% response rate. The questionnaire used a seven-point Likert scale to measure GSCM, GI, and environmental performance, with each construct measured using eight items. Data were analysed using SPSS, descriptive statistics, ordinary least squares regression, and moderation analysis. The direct relationships of GSCM and GI with environmental performance were examined, while the moderating effect of GI was assessed using the GSCM × GI interaction term. Results: GSCM had a positive and statistically significant relationship with environmental performance (B = 0.554, p < .001, R² = .339). GI also had a positive and statistically significant relationship with environmental performance (B = 0.414, p < .001, R² = .212). The interaction between GSCM and GI was positive and statistically significant (B = 0.365, p < .001), indicating that GI strengthens the positive relationship between GSCM and environmental performance. The interaction term accounted for an additional 11.1% of the explained variance in environmental performance (ΔR² = .111). Simple-slopes analysis showed that the GSCM–environmental performance relationship was positive but not statistically significant at low levels of GI, and positive and statistically significant at the mean and high levels of GI. The findings therefore provide empirical support for all three study objectives. Conclusion: GSCM and GI are positively associated with environmental performance among firms in Ghana’s agro-processing sector. More importantly, the positive relationship between GSCM and environmental performance becomes stronger at higher levels of green innovation. The findings suggest that firms may derive greater environmental benefits from green supply chain practices when these practices are supported by strong green innovation capabilities. Integrating GSCM with green innovation may therefore provide a more effective approach to improving environmental performance in the agro-processing sector.

title: Blockchain research in accounting and auditing through bibliometric and science mapping analysis
summary: Blockchain technology is increasingly reshaping industrial and organizational processes through its capacity to enhance transparency, traceability, automation, and data integrity. Within accounting and auditing, blockchain has emerged as a disruptive digital infrastructure capable of transforming financial reporting, assurance practices, governance mechanisms, and sustainability-related disclosure systems. Despite rapidly growing scholarly attention, the intellectual structure, interdisciplinary evolution, and emerging trajectories of blockchain research in accounting and auditing remain fragmented and insufficiently mapped. This study addresses this gap through a large-scale scientometric analysis of 322 peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus between 2017 and 2024. Using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer, the study examines publication and citation trends, leading authors, journals, institutions, and countries, international collaboration patterns, keyword co-occurrence networks, and the major thematic clusters represented in the literature. The findings reveal a rapidly expanding and globally interconnected research domain characterized by four dominant thematic areas: blockchain adoption in accounting and auditing, the impact of blockchain adoption on accounting and auditing practices, blockchain-enabled sustainability and governance, and the future integration of blockchain with artificial intelligence, Industry 4.0, and data-driven auditing environments. The analysis further identifies emerging research frontiers related to digital governance, continuous auditing, cybersecurity, intelligent supply chains, and technology-enabled accountability systems. The study contributes by providing a comprehensive computational overview of blockchain-enabled accounting ecosystems and by identifying critical knowledge gaps, interdisciplinary linkages, and future research directions relevant to researchers, regulators, audit firms, and technology-driven organizations. The findings highlight blockchain’s growing role as a foundational infrastructure for next-generation industrial and financial information systems.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Profitability of Listed Companies: Evidence from Haier Smart Home
summary: With the development of the digital economy, many manufacturing enterprises have begun to promote their own modernisation by going digital to enhance competitiveness. Haier Smart Home is a typical enterprise in the home appliance industry selected as the research object. A combination of case studies and financial indicator analysis will be used to explore the path and results of corporate profitability under digitalisation in this paper. The three areas of change that have reduced unit operating costs and period expense ratios for Haier Smart Home are intelligent manufacturing, supply chain digitalisation and user operation digitalisation. The above measures have increased gross margin and net margin by improving operating efficiency. At the same time, this paper also identifies problems in the process of digitalisation, such as high investment costs, weak business cooperation, and data security risks. Targeted Recommendations are then proposed. This paper adds to the body of research on the effect of digitalisation on corporate performance and provides a reference for manufacturing enterprises' digitalisation efforts.

title: The Social Architecture of Green Technology Governance: Digital Transformation, Labor Stratification and Green Digital Education in China’s High-Tech Sector
summary: Against China’s dual carbon strategic agenda and the deep integration of digital economy and real manufacturing, green technological innovation has long been framed as an industrial economic driver for high-tech sectors. Yet insufficient scholarly attention has been paid to its intertwined social, labour and educational repercussions—core domains of social science research. Digital transformation and environmental regulation jointly reshape corporate green innovation incentives, while simultaneously restructuring labour markets, widening inter-regional social inequalities, and exposing systemic gaps in public green digital literacy education. Drawing on balanced provincial panel data covering 30 Chinese provincial-level high-tech industries from 2012 to 2022, this study constructs multi-dimensional composite indicators of digital transformation and environmental regulatory stringency via the entropy weight method. It empirically estimates the baseline impact of industrial digitalisation on green innovation, and systematically unpacks the moderating social mechanisms embedded within environmental policy enforcement. Heterogeneity analyses are implemented across high-tech sub-sectors and three major geographic zones (Eastern, Central, Western China). Macro panel findings are triangulated with micro firm-level questionnaire data, and three robustness strategies (variable substitution, instrumental variable estimation, lagged variable processing) mitigate endogeneity bias. The empirical results reveal three interlinked economic-socio-educational outcomes: (1) Digital transformation significantly raises both the quantity and quality of green patents within hightech industries by reducing information frictions and optimising cross-regional innovation resource allocation, yet it exacerbates labour skill stratification and creates uneven access to digital green training resources across regions; (2) Environmental regulatory intensity positively moderates the digitalisation-green innovation linkage, consistent with an extended Porter Hypothesis contextualised to digital societies; stringent environmental compliance pressures push firms to invest in digital low-carbon upgrades, but simultaneously erode employment security for low-skilled workers and highlight underinvestment in vocational green technology education; (3) Pronounced industrial and regional social heterogeneity exists: synergies between digital transformation and environmental governance (alongside associated labour and educational pressures) are most salient in electronic information manufacturing and Eastern coastal provinces, whereas aerospace manufacturing and Western inland regions fail to realise equitable green transition outcomes due to inadequate digital infrastructure and under-resourced public environmental education systems. This paper reconceptualises digital-green industrial dynamics through sociological stratification theory and public policy education frameworks, expanding the theoretical scope of the Porter Hypothesis into social science discourse. Beyond industrial policy recommendations, it delivers transferable global insights for inclusive labour governance and green digital curriculum design, offering cross-national lessons for social scientists and education practitioners studying sustainable industrial transitions.

AI.abstract_translation: 在中国“双碳”战略议程以及数字经济与实体制造业深度融合的背景下，绿色技术创新长期被界定为高科技产业的产业经济驱动力。然而，学界对其交织的社会、劳动与教育影响——社会科学研究的核心领域——关注不足。数字化转型与环境监管共同重塑了企业绿色创新激励，同时也在重构劳动力市场、扩大区域间社会不平等，并暴露出公共绿色数字素养教育中的系统性缺口。本研究基于2012至2022年覆盖中国30个省级高科技产业的平衡面板数据，通过熵权法构建数字化转型与环境监管严格程度的多维综合指标。研究实证估计了产业数字化对绿色创新的基准影响，并系统解析了环境政策执行中所嵌入的调节性社会机制。异质性分析在高科技细分行业与三大地理区域（中国东部、中部、西部）之间展开。宏观面板发现与企业层面的微观问卷数据相互印证，并采用三种稳健性策略（变量替换、工具变量估计、滞后变量处理）以缓解内生性偏误。实证结果揭示了三个相互关联的经济—社会—教育结果：（1）数字化转型通过降低信息摩擦、优化跨区域创新资源配置，显著提升了高科技产业绿色专利的数量与质量，但它同时加剧了劳动技能分层，并造成各区域在数字绿色培训资源获取上的不均衡；（2）环境监管强度正向调节数字化—绿色创新之间的联系，这与拓展至数字社会的波特假说相一致；严格的环境合规压力推动企业投资于数字低碳升级，但同时削弱了低技能劳动者的就业保障，并凸显出职业绿色技术教育投入不足；（3）存在显著的产业与区域社会异质性：数字化转型与环境治理之间的协同效应（以及相关的劳动与教育压力）在电子信息制造业和东部沿海省份最为突出，而航空航天制造业与西部内陆地区则由于数字基础设施不足和公共环境教育体系资源匮乏，未能实现公平的绿色转型结果。本文通过社会学分层理论与公共政策教育框架重新概念化数字—绿色产业动态，将波特假说的理论范围拓展至社会科学话语之中。除产业政策建议之外，本文还为包容性劳动治理与绿色数字课程设计提供了可迁移的全球洞见，为研究可持续产业转型的社会科学家与教育实践者提供了跨国借鉴。
AI.tldr: 本文基于2012—2022年中国30个省级高科技产业的平衡面板数据并结合企业问卷数据，考察产业数字化转型如何通过降低信息摩擦和优化跨区域创新资源配置影响绿色创新的数量与质量，以及环境监管强度在其中的调节作用。结果表明数字化转型显著提升绿色专利的数量与质量，但加剧劳动技能分层和区域间数字绿色培训资源获取不均；环境监管强度正向调节数字化—绿色创新关系，且上述效应在电子信息制造业和东部沿海省份最为突出。
AI.motivation: 研究问题：在“双碳”战略与数字经济同实体制造业深度融合的背景下，数字化转型与环境监管如何共同塑造高科技产业的绿色技术创新，以及其伴随的劳动、社会与教育后果是什么。理论/研究背景：绿色技术创新长期被框定为高科技产业的产业经济驱动力，但摘要明确指出，学界对其交织的社会、劳动与教育影响关注不足。理论框架：摘要提及以社会学分层理论与公共政策教育框架重新概念化数字—绿色产业动态，并将波特假说拓展至数字社会情境。
AI.method: 数据与样本：2012至2022年中国30个省级高科技产业的平衡面板数据，并配合企业层面微观问卷数据。核心变量/研究对象：数字化转型与环境监管严格程度的多维综合指标（经熵权法构建）、绿色专利数量与质量、劳动技能分层、数字绿色培训资源获取、就业保障与职业绿色技术教育投入。研究方法：采用熵权法构建综合指标，实证估计产业数字化对绿色创新的基准影响，解析环境政策执行中的调节性社会机制，并在高科技细分行业与东部、中部、西部三大地理区域开展异质性分析；以问卷数据进行宏观与微观互证，并采用变量替换、工具变量估计、滞后变量处理三种稳健性策略缓解内生性偏误。
AI.result: 主要结论：（1）数字化转型通过降低信息摩擦、优化跨区域创新资源配置，显著提升高科技产业绿色专利的数量与质量，但同时加剧劳动技能分层，并造成区域间数字绿色培训资源获取不均；（2）调节效应：环境监管强度正向调节数字化与绿色创新之间的联系，这与情境化于数字社会的拓展版波特假说一致；严格的环境合规压力推动企业投资数字低碳升级，同时削弱低技能劳动者的就业保障并凸显职业绿色技术教育投入不足；（3）异质性：存在显著的产业与区域社会异质性，数字化转型与环境治理的协同效应及相关劳动与教育压力在电子信息制造业和东部沿海省份最为突出，而航空航天制造业与西部内陆地区因数字基础设施不足和公共环境教育体系资源匮乏，未能实现公平的绿色转型结果。
AI.conclusion: 理论/文献贡献：本文通过社会学分层理论与公共政策教育框架重新概念化数字—绿色产业动态，将波特假说的理论范围拓展至社会科学话语之中。实践/政策启示：在产业政策建议之外，本文为包容性劳动治理与绿色数字课程设计提供可迁移的全球洞见，并为研究可持续产业转型的社会科学家与教育实践者提供跨国借鉴；摘要亦指出数字基础设施不足与公共环境教育体系资源匮乏地区未能实现公平的绿色转型结果。
